elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New 12.c: "TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates" — express defence duty extending to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 12.c indemnifies "Client and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: 12.c(i): "an allegation that the Interface, the related software, the Hosting Services or the Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right" — tracks the deliverable/service set of this agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: 12.c(ii): "TrueLink's violation of any applicable law, rule or regulation".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: 12.c(iii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: "The party seeking indemnification under this Section 12 shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: "the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: "the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation in such defense".

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Amended 12.a limbs reduced to "(i) any claim arising out of or relating to the Client Content, and (ii) any violation by Client of any applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation"; the former breach-of-Agreement, customer-acts, Web Site and product-liability limbs are deleted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: 12.c(i) provides the third-party IP infringement/misappropriation indemnity in favour of Client.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-modification exclusion is inserted, and none is required, so the condition does not bite against the customer.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion inserted, which is at least as favourable to Customer as the fallback allows.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion inserted.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered 12.a–12.c language.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy is inserted.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No liability super-cap (3× annual fees) is added or cross-referenced; the comment expressly declines to import one.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate listing of the same fallback element; satisfied by 12.c(i).

reasons: All ten preferred elements are present in operative language: new Section 12.c supplies the defend-and-indemnify obligation to Client and affiliates for third-party IP infringement, TrueLink's breach of law, TrueLink-caused unauthorised access/disclosure and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus notice, control-of-defence and reasonable-cooperation mechanics; amended 12.a narrows the Client indemnity to Client Content and Client's violations of law.
The fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund remedy, no 3× annual-fee super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is fully satisfied.

Minimality holds: the insertion tracks the playbook model language without survival tails, own-expense language, extra damages categories or settlement-consent add-ons, and the favourable existing 12.b TrueLink indemnity for breach of the Agreement is retained rather than displaced. Deletions in 12.a are exactly those required by the Customer-indemnity-narrowing element.
Intent is preserved: 12.b and the mutual structure of Section 12 survive without contradiction, and 12.c's procedure is scoped to "this Section 12" so it operates consistently for both directions.

Drafting caution (not a defect against the checklist): 12.c(iii) references "Credit Data", which is not shown as a defined term in the resolved definitions; confirm it is defined in the Agreement (or change to a defined equivalent such as consumer credit information) to avoid an undefined term.
